title: Tuesday, July 28, 2026
description: Three things for the desk: the oil price collapse after the Iran ceasefire has taken the heat out of mortgage rates (30-year at 6.80%), but the Fed decides Wednesday at 2pm and the market is split roughly down the middle on hold versus hike — cuts are off the table entirely, so the risk of not locking is asymmetric; Fannie and Freddie eliminate the limited condo review on August 3rd, six days out, meaning every August condo closing needs a full review; and New Jersey has now seen over 10,800 announced job cuts this year, concentrated in Englewood Cliffs, Newark and Jersey City — watch those submarkets for autumn listing volume. And for the world: the US and Iran have stopped shooting but disagree publicly on whether talks exist; 330,000+ evacuated in the worst French and Spanish fire season on record; and Monday's chip selloff was about Chinese lithography advances, not AI spending.

title: Monday, July 27, 2026
description: Three things for the desk: mortgage rates hit a one-year high at roughly 6.75% with the Fed meeting Wednesday and the market pricing a hike rather than a cut; New Jersey is splitting by product type, with Essex single-family selling at 112% of list in 23 days while Hudson County condos sit at 42 days; and Fannie and Freddie eliminate limited condo reviews on August 3rd, adding an estimated $1,000+ per loan. Also today: New York State median price set a record at $475,000, Manhattan rents hit a record $5,295, landlords sued the NYC Rent Guidelines Board over the Mamdani rent freeze, US-Iran strikes paused for a second day, 300,000+ evacuated in French and Spanish wildfires, and Mourinho opened his second Real Madrid spell with a 1-0 win.
